paradigm.value: vt2: the rare wrist is always the right wrist and always the target (ANN18)
paradigm.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). (GUG18). The frozen VT2 follows ANN18 instead: 'instructed to mentally count the stimuli presented on the right wrist' (ANN18 Methods).
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (Front Neurosci 12:370; PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: Unlike the other two paradigms, it is a passive paradigm, and can yield EP differences to target vs. non-target stimuli even if the patient is not actively participating. [...] Importantly, the majority of the paradigms were based on oddball tasks that do not distinguish between active versus passive cortical responses.
second_classifier.source: GU17 Discussion; CH18 Discussion (ANN18 Methods for the VT2 layout)
second_classifier.note: VT2 is the passive oddball. GU17 says it yields target/non-target differences without active participation, so it does not show top-down engagement. ANN18's fixed right-wrist target also departs from GUG18's VT2, where the target wrist varies across sequences. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

timing.value: mur20: 100-ms pulse + 100-ms pause (SOA 200 ms), 4 instruction pauses of 13.5 s [derived], run ~157 s
timing.quote: GUG18 states the pulse and the run length but not the ISI or the pause length: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' MUR20 supplies the pause: 'All vibrotactile stimuli lasted 100 ms with a 100 ms pause between stimuli. The whole paradigm (i.e., one run) required around 2.5 min per run.' Consistent with every GUG18-stated timing item.
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; MUR20 (PMC7161577), Methods 'Paradigm' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: All vibrotactile stimuli lasted 100 ms with a 100 ms pause between stimuli. The whole paradigm (i.e., one run) required around 2.5 min per run.
second_classifier.note: 100-ms pulse + 100-ms pause and a ~2.5-min run are stated (480 stimuli, 60 groups of 8). The 13.5-s instruction pauses are derived to fill the stated run length, not stated. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

feat.value: seg8: −100 to 600 ms, 8 equal-segment means, no baseline
feat.quote: Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4a); baseline NOT STATED

second_classifier.quote: Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
second_classifier.note: Stated by GUG18, which describes no baseline step for the classifier features. ANN18 baseline-corrects its features, and MUR20/GU17 baseline-correct the plotted EPs. Under a co-equal reading, NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

second_classifier.quote: In VT2 run 1, the mean accuracy was only 20%, but was 50% for the first VT3 run. [...] P7 achieved a median accuracy of 20% in the first run and 90% in the best run.
second_classifier.note: No pipeline paper uses the full-test-pool point as the run statistic; they report the mean or median of the curve. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

thr.value: gt23: accuracy > 0.23
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c)

second_classifier.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated).
second_classifier.source: GUG18 Methods (also MUR20 Results; GU17 Methods 'about 23%')
second_classifier.note: Stated significance threshold (GUG18, MUR20, GU17). ANN18 instead used 70% as its VT2 'above chance' gate, and CH18 a binomial test, so under a co-equal reading of the mbvt papers this would be NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

vt2_mur20_seg8_full_gt23.eligibility_rule: union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity)
vt2_mur20_seg8_full_gt23.note: Ineligible: both classifiers CONTRADICTS on paradigm. One classifier only: second classifier CONTRADICTS on summary. NOT_STATED readings (primary) on timing, summary. cannot_call = false (min attainable p = 0 <= .05). low_coverage = not determined. Constant (all variants, not classified): N_GROUPS = 60 (4 instructions × 15 groups; GUG17 'four times', MUR20 '60 groups of 8'), whereas GUG18 states both 'Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli' and 15 targets per instruction (internally inconsistent); 10-20 substitutes for CP1/CP2/CPz (P3/P4/Pz) and 7 instead of 8 channels; the ±100 µV rejection and the 10 split-halves are STATED (GUG18). Patient composites (not variant axes): ge1_run = GUG18's stated 'for at least one run'; best60 (MUR20) and the ANN18 70% gates depart from GUG18's 23% rule. Convention: the paper is the reference. STATED = the paper states the value (for CORE-EXACT pipelines, where the paper is silent, the authors' public code counts, tagged -CODE). CONTRADICTS = departs from a value the paper states, including where the authors' code itself departs from the paper. Only axes that vary across this pipeline's variants are classified; constant departures are listed here and do not affect eligibility. cannot_call per bench.wrappers.min_attainable_p (the value the frozen 114 rows carry); low_coverage is empirical (115 coverage_of on result rows) and was not determined: no result files were opened. Eligibility = union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity); see 'second_classifier'.

summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve

CONTRADICTS stands: no grid variant uses CH18's VTP design ('duration = 110 ms, ISI = 300 ms', §2.3.3) or its features ('an average was performed on every 12 samples for each EEG channel, resulting in 15 new sample points', §2.4), so the variant pairs CH18's n with GUG18 / MUR20 / ANN18 settings, against GUG18's stated 23%.

paradigm.value: vt2: the rare wrist is always the right wrist and always the target (ANN18)
paradigm.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). (GUG18). second_classifier.quote: Unlike the other two paradigms, it is a passive paradigm, and can yield EP differences to target vs. non-target stimuli even if the patient is not actively participating. timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: The employed oddball paradigms administered mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.

feat.value: ds7: 0 to 600 ms down-sampled to 7, baseline −100 to 0 ms (ANN18)
feat.quote: GUG18: 'Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. ANN18: 'The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.' ds7 departs from GUG18's stated 8 segments over −100 to 600 ms.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments. summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

CONTRADICTS stands: no grid variant uses CH18's VTP design ('duration = 110 ms, ISI = 300 ms', §2.3.3) or its features ('an average was performed on every 12 samples for each EEG channel, resulting in 15 new sample points', §2.4), so the variant pairs CH18's n with GUG18 / MUR20 / ANN18 settings, against GUG18's stated 23%.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c); CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.3.3, §2.4, §2.5

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').

feat.value: ds7: 0 to 600 ms down-sampled to 7, baseline −100 to 0 ms (ANN18)
feat.quote: GUG18: 'Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

second_classifier.quote: In VT2 run 1, the mean accuracy was only 20%, but was 50% for the first VT3 run. [...] P7 achieved a median accuracy of 20% in the first run and 90% in the best run.
second_classifier.note: No paper uses the curve maximum (MUR20's 'maximum' is across runs). This is a more liberal statistic than the stated mean or median. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

thr.value: binom_n10: accuracy >= 0.4000 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 10 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 40.0% departs from it.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c)

second_classifier.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated).
second_classifier.source: GUG18 Methods (also MUR20 Results: 'above chance level (>23%)')

vt2_ann18_ds7_max_binom_n10.note: Ineligible: both classifiers CONTRADICTS on paradigm, feat, thr. One classifier only: primary CONTRADICTS on timing; second classifier CONTRADICTS on summary. NOT_STATED readings (primary) on summary. cannot_call = false (min attainable p = 0 <= .05). low_coverage = not determined. Constant (all variants, not classified): N_GROUPS = 60 (4 instructions × 15 groups; GUG17 'four times', MUR20 '60 groups of 8'), whereas GUG18 states both 'Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli' and 15 targets per instruction (internally inconsistent); 10-20 substitutes for CP1/CP2/CPz (P3/P4/Pz) and 7 instead of 8 channels; the ±100 µV rejection and the 10 split-halves are STATED (GUG18). Patient composites (not variant axes): ge1_run = GUG18's stated 'for at least one run'; best60 (MUR20) and the ANN18 70% gates depart from GUG18's 23% rule. Convention: the paper is the reference. STATED = the paper states the value (for CORE-EXACT pipelines, where the paper is silent, the authors' public code counts, tagged -CODE). CONTRADICTS = departs from a value the paper states, including where the authors' code itself departs from the paper. Only axes that vary across this pipeline's variants are classified; constant departures are listed here and do not affect eligibility. cannot_call per bench.wrappers.min_attainable_p (the value the frozen 114 rows carry); low_coverage is empirical (115 coverage_of on result rows) and was not determined: no result files were opened. Eligibility = union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity); see 'second_classifier'.

paradigm.value: vt2: the rare wrist is always the right wrist and always the target (ANN18)
paradigm.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). (GUG18). The frozen VT2 follows ANN18 instead: 'instructed to mentally count the stimuli presented on the right wrist' (ANN18 Methods).
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (Front Neurosci 12:370; PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: Unlike the other two paradigms, it is a passive paradigm, and can yield EP differences to target vs. non-target stimuli even if the patient is not actively participating. [...] Importantly, the majority of the paradigms were based on oddball tasks that do not distinguish between active versus passive cortical responses.
second_classifier.source: GU17 Discussion; CH18 Discussion (ANN18 Methods for the VT2 layout)
second_classifier.note: VT2 is the passive oddball. GU17 says it yields target/non-target differences without active participation, so it does not show top-down engagement. ANN18's fixed right-wrist target also departs from GUG18's VT2, where the target wrist varies across sequences. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: The employed oddball paradigms administered mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.
second_classifier.note: 30-ms pulses, 270-ms ISI (300-ms SOA), 480 stimuli in 2.4 min (= 144 s) are stated; 144 s leaves no time for instruction pauses, which is consistent with 0 s. ANN18 says both VT2 and VT3 take 2.4 min. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

feat.value: ds7: 0 to 600 ms down-sampled to 7, baseline −100 to 0 ms (ANN18)
feat.quote: GUG18: 'Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.' ANN18: 'The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.' ds7 departs from GUG18's stated 8 segments over −100 to 600 ms.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments. second_classifier.note: ANN18 states this feature set verbatim, but primary GUG18 states 8 equal-segment sub-averages, and CH18 a third variant (15 points of 12-sample averages). thr.value: binom_n30: accuracy >= 0.2667 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 30 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 26.7% departs from it. Source of n = 30: CH18 §2.5: 'We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).' CONTRADICTS stands: no grid variant uses CH18's VTP design ('duration = 110 ms, ISI = 300 ms', §2.3.3) or its features ('an average was performed on every 12 samples for each EEG channel, resulting in 15 new sample points', §2.4), so the variant pairs CH18's n with GUG18 / MUR20 / ANN18 settings, against GUG18's stated 23%.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c); CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.3.3, §2.4, §2.5

second_classifier.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). [...] We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).
second_classifier.note: Primary GUG18 states > 23%. CH18 does state a binomial p < .05 rule with n = 30 and chance 1/8 for VTP, which gives >= 8/30 = 26.67% one-sided (sidedness unstated), so this value reproduces CH18's rule. Under a co-equal reading, NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

second_classifier.quote: In VT2 run 1, the mean accuracy was only 20%, but was 50% for the first VT3 run. [...] P7 achieved a median accuracy of 20% in the first run and 90% in the best run.

thr.value: binom_n60: accuracy >= 0.2167 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 60 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 21.7% departs from it. Note: binom_n60 (>= 13/60 = 0.2167) gives the same calls as gt23 (> 0.23) under every summary: curve points are multiples of 0.1 (split_eval, reps = 10), so full and max are, and the median is a multiple of 0.05; no attainable accuracy lies in [0.2167, 0.23] [derived]. Class stays CONTRADICTS (the stated value is 23%).
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c)

paradigm.value: vt3: per group 1 left + 1 right + 6 distractors, instructed wrist = target, 2 left / 2 right instructions
paradigm.quote: Abstract: '(ii) VT3 with three vibro-tactile stimulators fixed on both wrists and on the back'. Methods: 'In both VT3 modes, one additional stimulator is fixed on the back or shoulder as a distractor, which is active in 75% of stimulations. The per-group composition and the pseudo-random, balanced target wrist are as stated; the group count (stated 30 groups, 15 left and 15 right targets; built 60 groups, 30 and 30) is a constant departure: see constant_departures.mbvt 'groups per run'.

second_classifier.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). [...] Each VT3 run contains 30 groups of 8 stimuli (30 left, 30 right, 180 distractors).

timing.value: mur20: 100-ms pulse + 100-ms pause (SOA 200 ms), 4 instruction pauses of 13.5 s [derived], run ~157 s
timing.quote: GUG18 states the pulse and the run length but not the ISI or the pause length: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4a); baseline NOT STATED

second_classifier.quote: Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
second_classifier.note: Stated by GUG18, which describes no baseline step for the classifier features. ANN18 baseline-corrects its features, and MUR20/GU17 baseline-correct the plotted EPs. Under a co-equal reading, NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

second_classifier.quote: In VT2 run 1, the mean accuracy was only 20%, but was 50% for the first VT3 run. [...] P7 achieved a median accuracy of 20% in the first run and 90% in the best run.
second_classifier.note: No pipeline paper uses the full-test-pool point as the run statistic; they report the mean or median of the curve. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

thr.value: gt23: accuracy > 0.23
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c)

second_classifier.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated).
second_classifier.source: GUG18 Methods (also MUR20 Results; GU17 Methods 'about 23%')
second_classifier.note: Stated significance threshold (GUG18, MUR20, GU17). ANN18 instead used 70% as its VT2 'above chance' gate, and CH18 a binomial test, so under a co-equal reading of the mbvt papers this would be NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

vt3_ann18_seg8_full_gt23.eligibility_rule: union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity)
vt3_ann18_seg8_full_gt23.note: Eligible (union). One classifier only: primary CONTRADICTS on timing; second classifier CONTRADICTS on summary (not strict). NOT_STATED readings (primary) on summary. cannot_call = false (min attainable p = 0 <= .05). low_coverage = not determined. Constant (all variants, not classified): N_GROUPS = 60 (4 instructions × 15 groups; GUG17 'four times', MUR20 '60 groups of 8'), whereas GUG18 states both 'Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli' and 15 targets per instruction (internally inconsistent); 10-20 substitutes for CP1/CP2/CPz (P3/P4/Pz) and 7 instead of 8 channels; the ±100 µV rejection and the 10 split-halves are STATED (GUG18). Patient composites (not variant axes): ge1_run = GUG18's stated 'for at least one run'; best60 (MUR20) and the ANN18 70% gates depart from GUG18's 23% rule. Convention: the paper is the reference. STATED = the paper states the value (for CORE-EXACT pipelines, where the paper is silent, the authors' public code counts, tagged -CODE). CONTRADICTS = departs from a value the paper states, including where the authors' code itself departs from the paper. Only axes that vary across this pipeline's variants are classified; constant departures are listed here and do not affect eligibility. cannot_call per bench.wrappers.min_attainable_p (the value the frozen 114 rows carry); low_coverage is empirical (115 coverage_of on result rows) and was not determined: no result files were opened. Eligibility = union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity); see 'second_classifier'.

paradigm.value: vt3: per group 1 left + 1 right + 6 distractors, instructed wrist = target, 2 left / 2 right instructions
paradigm.quote: Abstract: '(ii) VT3 with three vibro-tactile stimulators fixed on both wrists and on the back'. Methods: 'In both VT3 modes, one additional stimulator is fixed on the back or shoulder as a distractor, which is active in 75% of stimulations. The other two stimulators are again fixed on the right and left wrist and each receive 12.5% of the stimuli.' The per-group composition and the pseudo-random, balanced target wrist are as stated; the group count (stated 30 groups, 15 left and 15 right targets; built 60 groups, 30 and 30) is a constant departure: see constant_departures.mbvt 'groups per run'.
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Abstract and Methods 'BCI assessment' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). [...] Each VT3 run contains 30 groups of 8 stimuli (30 left, 30 right, 180 distractors).
second_classifier.source: GUG18 Methods (paradigms); ANN18 and MUR20 Methods agree
second_classifier.note: Stated VT3 structure: 12.5% left, 12.5% right, 75% distractor, instructed wrist is the target, equal left/right targets over 4 instructions. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: The employed oddball paradigms administered mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.
second_classifier.note: 30-ms pulses, 270-ms ISI (300-ms SOA), 480 stimuli in 2.4 min (= 144 s) are stated; 144 s leaves no time for instruction pauses, which is consistent with 0 s. ANN18 says both VT2 and VT3 take 2.4 min. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

thr.value: binom_n30: accuracy >= 0.2667 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 30 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 26.7% departs from it. Source of n = 30: CH18 §2.5: 'We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).' CONTRADICTS stands: no grid variant uses CH18's VTP design ('duration = 110 ms, ISI = 300 ms', §2.3.3) or its features ('an average was performed on every 12 samples for each EEG channel, resulting in 15 new sample points', §2.4), so the variant pairs CH18's n with GUG18 / MUR20 / ANN18 settings, against GUG18's stated 23%.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c); CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.3.3, §2.4, §2.5

second_classifier.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). [...] We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).
second_classifier.note: Primary GUG18 states > 23%. CH18 does state a binomial p < .05 rule with n = 30 and chance 1/8 for VTP, which gives >= 8/30 = 26.67% one-sided (sidedness unstated), so this value reproduces CH18's rule. Under a co-equal reading, NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

vt3_ann18_seg8_full_binom_n30.eligibility_rule: union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity)
vt3_ann18_seg8_full_binom_n30.note: Ineligible: both classifiers CONTRADICTS on thr. One classifier only: primary CONTRADICTS on timing; second classifier CONTRADICTS on summary. NOT_STATED readings (primary) on summary. cannot_call = false (min attainable p = 0 <= .05). low_coverage = not determined. Constant (all variants, not classified): N_GROUPS = 60 (4 instructions × 15 groups; GUG17 'four times', MUR20 '60 groups of 8'), whereas GUG18 states both 'Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli' and 15 targets per instruction (internally inconsistent); 10-20 substitutes for CP1/CP2/CPz (P3/P4/Pz) and 7 instead of 8 channels; the ±100 µV rejection and the 10 split-halves are STATED (GUG18). STATED = the paper states the value (for CORE-EXACT pipelines, where the paper is silent, the authors' public code counts, tagged -CODE). CONTRADICTS = departs from a value the paper states, including where the authors' code itself departs from the paper. Only axes that vary across this pipeline's variants are classified; constant departures are listed here and do not affect eligibility. cannot_call per bench.wrappers.min_attainable_p (the value the frozen 114 rows carry); low_coverage is empirical (115 coverage_of on result rows) and was not determined: no result files were opened. Eligibility = union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity); see 'second_classifier'.

paradigm.value: vt3: per group 1 left + 1 right + 6 distractors, instructed wrist = target, 2 left / 2 right instructions
paradigm.quote: Abstract: '(ii) VT3 with three vibro-tactile stimulators fixed on both wrists and on the back'. Methods: 'In both VT3 modes, one additional stimulator is fixed on the back or shoulder as a distractor, which is active in 75% of stimulations. The other two stimulators are again fixed on the right and left wrist and each receive 12.5% of the stimuli.' The per-group composition and the pseudo-random, balanced target wrist are as stated; the group count (stated 30 groups, 15 left and 15 right targets; built 60 groups, 30 and 30) is a constant departure: see constant_departures.mbvt 'groups per run'.
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Abstract and Methods 'BCI assessment' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). [...] Each VT3 run contains 30 groups of 8 stimuli (30 left, 30 right, 180 distractors).
second_classifier.source: GUG18 Methods (paradigms); ANN18 and MUR20 Methods agree
second_classifier.note: Stated VT3 structure: 12.5% left, 12.5% right, 75% distractor, instructed wrist is the target, equal left/right targets over 4 instructions. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: The employed oddball paradigms administered mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.
second_classifier.note: 30-ms pulses, 270-ms ISI (300-ms SOA), 480 stimuli in 2.4 min (= 144 s) are stated; 144 s leaves no time for instruction pauses, which is consistent with 0 s. ANN18 says both VT2 and VT3 take 2.4 min. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

feat.value: seg8: −100 to 600 ms, 8 equal-segment means, no baseline
feat.quote: Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.

Methods: 'In both VT3 modes, one additional stimulator is fixed on the back or shoulder as a distractor, which is active in 75% of stimulations. The other two stimulators are again fixed on the right and left wrist and each receive 12.5% of the stimuli.' The per-group composition and the pseudo-random, balanced target wrist are as stated; the group count (stated 30 groups, 15 left and 15 right targets; built 60 groups, 30 and 30) is a constant departure: see constant_departures.mbvt 'groups per run'.
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Abstract and Methods 'BCI assessment' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). [...] Each VT3 run contains 30 groups of 8 stimuli (30 left, 30 right, 180 distractors).
second_classifier.source: GUG18 Methods (paradigms); ANN18 and MUR20 Methods agree
second_classifier.note: Stated VT3 structure: 12.5% left, 12.5% right, 75% distractor, instructed wrist is the target, equal left/right targets over 4 instructions. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: The employed oddball paradigms administered mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.
second_classifier.note: 30-ms pulses, 270-ms ISI (300-ms SOA), 480 stimuli in 2.4 min (= 144 s) are stated; 144 s leaves no time for instruction pauses, which is consistent with 0 s. ANN18 says both VT2 and VT3 take 2.4 min. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

feat.value: ds7: 0 to 600 ms down-sampled to 7, baseline −100 to 0 ms (ANN18)
feat.quote: GUG18: 'Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.' ANN18: 'The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.' ds7 departs from GUG18's stated 8 segments over −100 to 600 ms.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods (cat. §4a)

second_classifier.quote: Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments. [...] Baseline correction was done using the 100 ms before stimulus onset. The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.
second_classifier.note: ANN18 states this feature set verbatim, but primary GUG18 states 8 equal-segment sub-averages, and CH18 a third variant (15 points of 12-sample averages). Under a co-equal reading of the mbvt papers this is NOT_STATED. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

summary.value: the maximum of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

second_classifier.quote: In VT2 run 1, the mean accuracy was only 20%, but was 50% for the first VT3 run. [...] P7 achieved a median accuracy of 20% in the first run and 90% in the best run.
second_classifier.note: No paper uses the curve maximum (MUR20's 'maximum' is across runs). This is a more liberal statistic than the stated mean or median. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

thr.value: binom_n60: accuracy >= 0.2167 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 60 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 21.7% departs from it. Note: binom_n60 (>= 13/60 = 0.2167) gives the same calls as gt23 (> 0.23) under every summary: curve points are multiples of 0.1 (split_eval, reps = 10), so full and max are, and the median is a multiple of 0.05; no attainable accuracy lies in [0.2167, 0.23] [derived]. Class stays CONTRADICTS (the stated value is 23%).
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c)

second_classifier.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated).
second_classifier.note: 21.67% is more lenient than the stated 23% and is not stated anywhere. mbvt has no eponymous paper; I took GUG18 (first-listed; the DoC VT paper that states the whole decision rule) as primary for features/threshold/summary/paradigm, and the paper named in the variant for the timing axis.

vt3_ann18_ds7_max_binom_n60.eligibility_rule: union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity)
vt3_ann18_ds7_max_binom_n60.note: Ineligible: both classifiers CONTRADICTS on feat, thr. One classifier only: primary CONTRADICTS on timing; second classifier CONTRADICTS on summary. NOT_STATED readings (primary) on summary. cannot_call = false (min attainable p = 0 <= .05). low_coverage = not determined. Constant (all variants, not classified): N_GROUPS = 60 (4 instructions × 15 groups; GUG17 'four times', MUR20 '60 groups of 8'), whereas GUG18 states both 'Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli' and 15 targets per instruction (internally inconsistent); 10-20 substitutes for CP1/CP2/CPz (P3/P4/Pz) and 7 instead of 8 channels; the ±100 µV rejection and the 10 split-halves are STATED (GUG18). Patient composites (not variant axes): ge1_run = GUG18's stated 'for at least one run'; best60 (MUR20) and the ANN18 70% gates depart from GUG18's 23% rule. Convention: the paper is the reference. STATED = the paper states the value (for CORE-EXACT pipelines, where the paper is silent, the authors' public code counts, tagged -CODE). CONTRADICTS = departs from a value the paper states, including where the authors' code itself departs from the paper. Only axes that vary across this pipeline's variants are classified; constant departures are listed here and do not affect eligibility. cannot_call per bench.wrappers.min_attainable_p (the value the frozen 114 rows carry); low_coverage is empirical (115 coverage_of on result rows) and was not determined: no result files were opened. Eligibility = union of two blind classifications (primary); strict = both agree (sensitivity); see 'second_classifier'.

second_classifier.quote: ITPC data indicates 100% sensitivity and 80% speciﬁcity for a distinction between bad outcome (death, VS/UWS) and good outcome at 6 months (GOSE > = 3; threshold = 0.116; see Fig 2D).
second_classifier.note: 0.116 is the paper's only per-patient cut-off on phrase/sentence ITPC. Caveat: it is a ROC cut chosen on 6-month outcome, not a detection threshold. It does target the top-down (phrase/sentence) rate.

mbvt.stated_value: 30 groups of 8; 15 left-target and 15 right-target groups (GUG18; the same paragraph also implies 4 x (15 + 105) = 480 stimuli)
mbvt.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). | Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. | Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli (120 left, 120 right). Each VT3 run contains 30 groups of 8 stimuli (30 left, 30 right, 180 distractors).
mbvt.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093), Methods 'BCI assessment' (three sentences of one paragraph, separated by ' | ')
mbvt.our_value: 60 groups (4 instructions x 15 groups, 480 stimuli; GUG17 'performs this task four times', MUR20 '480 stimuli per run, with 60 groups of 8 stimuli'): 30 left-target and 30 right-target groups in VT3, a 30-point test curve
mbvt.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); GUG18 is internally inconsistent here, and the curve length changes the null distribution of every summary

mbvt.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); expected small on a null (no evoked signal at any site); one fewer channel means fewer LDA features

mbvt.quote: The reference electrode was fixed on the right earlobe and the ground electrode was mounted on the forehead.
mbvt.our_value: the recording's own reference (BDSP / source montage), not re-referenced

mbvt.stated_value: remove target and non-target trials until the ratio is 1:7 again (MUR20)

mbvt.our_value: a whole group of 8 is dropped when any of its epochs is rejected (keeps 1:7 exactly; which trials MUR20 removed is NOT STATED)
mbvt.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); differs only on recordings with rejected epochs

errata.where: the erp catalogue §6 (GIB16), SSEP F-test quote
errata.error: The catalogue quoted 'An F ratio (alpha=.05; F2,20>=3.49) was computed to compare the power at 5 and 10 Hz with the average power in the ten adjacent ~1 Hz frequency bins' and stopped before the parenthesis that names the bins. The frozen gibson16 module therefore treated the noise bins as NOT STATED and froze two readings ('plain', 'nonharm'), neither of which matches the stated set.
errata.aam_quote: An F ratio (alpha=.05; F2,20>=3.49) was computed to compare the power at 5 and 10 Hz with the average power in the ten adjacent ~1 Hz frequency bins (2-4 Hz, 6-9 Hz, and 11-13 Hz)39.
errata.source: GIB16 author accepted manuscript (Kent KAR), 'Page 8 of 42'
errata.consequence: All 4 gibson16 SSEP variants are CONTRADICTS on 'bins' (correction accepted by the lead). The catalogue file itself was not edited (read-only for this task).
